research.facts:
Kawhi Leonard Investigation Could Drag Into 2027
**Facts (HIGH confidence — multiple independent sources):**
- NBA investigation began September 2025, now in its 11th month
- Probe examines whether Clippers circumvented salary cap via Aspiration Partners Inc. endorsement deal: $28 million over 4 years to Kawhi Leonard, plus reportedly $20 million in Aspiration equity
- Aspiration Partners also had a $300 million, 23-year naming rights deal with the Clippers
- NBA's outside law firm has completed its fact-finding phase
research.sources:
- Sources at ESPN, HoopsHype, Yahoo Sports, and OpenCourt Basketball (published July 29-30) say investigation could extend into 2027
- NBPA can demand CBA arbitration before any penalty is imposed — this is the key delay mechanism
- Clippers claim they were victims of fraud, not co-conspirators
- Aspiration CEO convicted and sentenced to 14 years in federal prison for wire fraud
- Commissioner Silver has publicly said probe must conclude before 2026-27 season starts (now in question)
- Proposed Raptors-Clippers trade: Toronto gets Leonard; Clippers get Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, a 2027 first-round pick swap, two second-round picks
- Trade is officially on hold; NBA will not allow it to close until probe resolves
- Kawhi Leonard and Clippers both deny wrongdoing
- Sources: ESPN (espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49482792), HoopsHype, OpenCourt Basketball, Yahoo Sports, FOX LA
**Facts (MEDIUM confidence — single sources):**
- Raptors still cannot plan their 2026-27 roster with this uncertainty
- If both sides cannot agree on settlement, case goes to neutral arbitrator jointly appointed by NBA and NBPA

research.facts:
DeMar DeRozan Returns to Chicago Bulls
**Facts (HIGH confidence — NBA.com, Bulls official page, multiple outlets):**
- DeRozan waived by Sacramento Kings on July 6, 2026, making him a free agent
- DeRozan originally joined Kings via sign-and-trade in July 2024 (3yr/$73.89M reported)
- Multiple teams expressed interest: Miami Heat, Denver Nuggets, Cleveland Cavaliers, Washington Wizards
- League sources (per Threads/@theboxscoreph) report DeRozan signing 2-year, $30 million deal to return to Chicago Bulls
- Bulls official page at nba.com/bulls/news references DeRozan acquisition
- DeRozan, 36, had his best post-prime seasons in Chicago (averaged 24.5 PPG, 4.9 APG across 4 seasons with Bulls)
- Bulls 2025-26 head coach: Torsten Splitter (one of six new coaches named this offseason)
**Facts (MEDIUM confidence — conflicting reports):**
- Contract value: League sources via Threads say $30M/2yr ($15M per year)
- Earlier reports (Yahoo Sports, Bleacher Report) said $80M/2yr ($40M per year) — this appears to be inaccurate
- No official press release from Bulls or Shams/Woj confirmation found as of July 30
- DeRozan's motivations: chose Chicago over other suitors (specifics unconfirmed)

research.facts:
Victor Wembanyama's $252M Extension and San Antonio's Strategy
**Facts (HIGH confidence — NBC Sports, NBA.com, multiple outlets):**
- Wembanyama signed 5-year, $252 million max rookie-scale extension with San Antonio Spurs
- The 25% max, NOT the 30% supermax
- Supermax would have been approximately $303 million
- Difference: ~$51 million left on the table intentionally
- Spurs also signed/committed to De'Aaron Fox (traded for; 4yr/$228M extension)
- Other Spurs commitments: Stephon Castle (~$10M), Ron Holland (~$13M/yr), Harrison Ingram (~$5M)
- Wemby's reasoning (per reports): cap flexibility to build winning team around him
- Wemby is 22 years old (born January 4, 2004)
- Spurs head coach: unconfirmed for 2026-27 (coaching staff in transition)
**Facts (MEDIUM confidence):**
- Specific numbers for secondary Spurs players sourced from story history (pipeline notes July 26); should be treated as approximate
